solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seconds a beanpole may welcome?

blocks.note: first meaning: those who finish second in a contest
second meaning, read as two words: runner beans climbing up a pole

explanation.surface: A tall thin person is offered a second helping and gladly accepts.
explanation.walkthrough: A beanpole looks like a lanky person, but here it is the garden cane that runner beans grow up, so RUNNERS UP is what it welcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up are the competitors who take second place, so they are the seconds in a race.

clue.text: Put back initially rumpled bedsheets evenly

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only of the following word
evenly asks for the letters in the even positions, second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: first letter of rumpled
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of bedsheets

explanation.surface: Someone tidies a bed by putting the crumpled sheets back straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set or put it back to an earlier position.

clue.text: One might net flounder in darker hours

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle about clumsily, so the letters before it tumble out of order

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fisherman might land a flounder in his net after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Flounder looks like the fish being netted, but it is a verb telling the letters to thrash about.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-time is the period of darkness, the hours after the sun has set.

clue.text: Soothing Hardy book borders on eroticism at the start

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
tells the solver to put the piece from the edges of the word at the front of the build

blocks.note: the first and last letters of eroticism
Oliver Hardy, of Laurel and Hardy, was known as Ollie
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A soothing novel by Thomas Hardy skirts the edges of eroticism from its opening pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy suggests Thomas Hardy the novelist, but it is the comedian Oliver Hardy, nicknamed Ollie.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is something that soothes and softens, like a skin cream or calming words.

clue.text: Giddy habit going on in baths?

blocks.note: when you feel giddy your head is swimming
a habit is a style of dress, a costume

explanation.surface: A dizzying habit of always heading off to the public baths.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a swimming costume is what goes on your body when you go into the baths, the British word for a public swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming costume is the garment a swimmer puts on before getting into the pool.

clue.text: State protection from capitalism? You'll go nuts!

indicators.note: to go nuts is to go mad, so the letters lose their order and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dissident warns that living under capitalism will drive you mad, so seek protection from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Political asylum is the protection a country grants to a refugee fleeing persecution at home.

clue.text: Clips for bracelets

blocks.note: first meaning: light blows, as in clips round the ear
second meaning: slang for handcuffs, which are called bracelets by the police

explanation.walkthrough: Clips and bracelets suggest jewellery; in fact both are slang, one for slaps and one for handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff someone is to hit them lightly, and cuffs is a common short form of handcuffs.

clue.text: Pole thrown from vehicle sheltering to live

indicators.note: something sheltering another holds it safely inside itself

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A pole is flung out of a car in which someone is living rough.
explanation.walkthrough: The caber is the long tree trunk tossed in Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the heavy wooden pole hurled end over end in the Scottish sport of tossing the caber.

clue.text: Composer's refrain?

blocks.note: first meaning: Manuel de ..., the Spanish composer
second meaning: fa-la, the nonsense chorus of old songs

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, so the composer is a refrain: fa-la, as in fa-la-la, sung as a chorus in madrigals and carols.
explanation.definitionFit: Falla wrote The Three-Cornered Hat, and fa-la is the traditional burden or chorus of nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Couple heard in enclosure: "About to get fat!"

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that only sounds like the one meaning a couple
in places one piece inside the enclosing word

blocks.note: a sty is a pig's enclosure
a couple is a pair, which sounds like pare
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a couple in a pen announcing they are about to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is everyday slang for a roll of fat round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is a bulge of excess fat around the middle, likened to an extra wheel.

clue.text: Maybe Leo and Boris, at heart, are men of Roman stamp?

indicators.note: maybe flags that the word after it is one example of a wider class
the heart of a word is its central part, with the edges trimmed

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
the middle letters of Boris

explanation.surface: Two men named Leo and Boris are said to be true Romans at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo and Boris look like a pair of men; Leo is in fact a star sign and only the middle of Boris is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural for gentlemen, so it names men from Rome or Italy.

clue.text: Direction signs installed in Louisiana plant

indicators.note: something installed in a place is fitted inside it

blocks.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana
obeli are dagger marks in printing that direct the reader to a footnote

explanation.surface: Road signs are being put up in the US state of Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: An obelus (plural obeli) is the dagger symbol used as a reference mark in text, not a road sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flower, often blue, grown in hanging baskets and borders.

clue.text: Tug's noise cut conversation outright

indicators.note: cut means each word around it is shortened by losing its ending

blocks.note: a tugboat sounds a toot on its horn
talk is conversation

explanation.surface: The noise of a tug's horn interrupts a conversation completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are trimmed: the toot loses its last two letters and the talk its last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright and total are synonyms meaning complete or absolute, as in a total failure.

clue.text: Ohio Democrat stumbles in procession

indicators.note: one who stumbles loses footing, so the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for Ohio
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician from Ohio trips while marching in a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, typically escorting a dignitary.

clue.text: Drive away from outskirts of Eastbourne around eleven-fifty

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters count
around makes the edge letters wrap about the numbers that follow

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Eastbourne
XI is eleven in Roman numerals
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone drives out of the edge of Eastbourne, a south-coast English seaside town, at ten to twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven-fifty looks like a clock time, but it is two Roman numerals side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, driving them away from their homeland.

clue.text: Lapse I put right involving "PC" Scottish Church

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective in the church's name, the Scottish Episcopal Church

indicators.note: putting something right means rearranging it into proper order
involving means wrapping round and taking in the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a PC, police constable, is a cop

explanation.surface: A police officer corrects a slip involving a Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around PC hint that it stands for a word: a PC is a cop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Episcopal Church is Scotland's Anglican church, governed by bishops, hence the name.

clue.text: Need change of scene? It's the Fourth of July!

indicators.note: a change of something alters it, so these letters take a new order
the fourth of a word is its fourth letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
the fourth letter of July

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a change of surroundings on American Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fourth of July looks like the US holiday but means only the fourth letter of the word July.
explanation.definitionFit: A necessity is something needed, an essential requirement.

clue.text: Assistant priest to prosecute a cheat about degree

indicators.note: about means going round the outside of the next piece

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
BD, Bachelor of Divinity, is a degree
taken as written
a con is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A junior cleric is taking a fraudster to court over a fake degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the degree used is the Bachelor of Divinity, a churchman's qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric ranking below a deacon, who assists the priest at services.

clue.text: Sickness from crummy toast

blocks.note: crummy means poor or bad, as does ill
a toast is drunk to someone's health

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick after eating crumbly, poor-quality toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Crummy suggests crumbs on the bread, and toast the bread; really one means bad and the other is a drink to someone's good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is a state of being unwell, so it is another word for sickness.

clue.text: Duplicate study into development of iliac trouble having no currency

indicators.note: having no means a word sheds the letters named after it
a development of something reshapes it, so these letters rearrange
into places the first piece inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a den is a study, a room for working in
taken as written
taken as written
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A medical student studies an outbreak of hip trouble that left a patient penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: Trouble without its rouble leaves only T, which joins iliac to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicate as an adjective means exactly alike, a matching copy.

clue.text: German in ill humour? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: bile is one of the old humours and stands for bad temper
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A grumpy German dismisses something as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge, the dirty water in a ship's hull, is slang for rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Cleansing moggies is mostly difficult inside

indicators.note: mostly means all of the word except its last letter
inside places the shortened word within the other pieces

blocks.note: moggies are cats, a moggy being British slang for a cat; then is as written
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Bathing cats is generally a difficult job.
explanation.walkthrough: A moggy is everyday British slang for a cat, usually a mongrel one.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is a purging or emotional cleansing, from the Greek for purification.

clue.text: Note – amateur artist's making crown

blocks.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
A is the abbreviation for amateur
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A message saying a hobby painter is making a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled head ornament, a small crown worn by women.

clue.text: A date coming up in the theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a and an are the same article
a date can mean a period of history, an era

explanation.surface: A romantic date is coming up at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a scene of activity, just as a theatre of war is a field of operations.

clue.text: Vessels were off to Sweden

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are spoilt and jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the international code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Ships set sail for Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels and off together suggest ships departing; vessels are really jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large jugs with wide spouts, vessels for holding water.

clue.text: Moans'll be heard with material for painter, say?

indicators.note: be heard means the answer is spelt as these words sound when spoken

blocks.note: moans are sighs, so moans will is sighs'll

explanation.surface: An artist will be heard groaning about the materials they work with.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter is not an artist but a boat's painter, the rope used to tie it up; sisal fibre makes rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a strong plant fibre used to make rope, such as the line called a painter.

clue.text: Levelling off metalware with gold

blocks.note: plate is household ware of silver or gold
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone levels off a polished metal ornament with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: a plateau is a levelling off, as in prices reaching a plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a stage where growth stops and things stay at a steady level.

clue.text: Counsel a coloratura somewhat when returning with spots

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used
returning means going back, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the letters running through the end of counsel, a, and the start of coloratura

explanation.surface: A vocal coach gives a coloratura soprano some advice after she comes back with a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Locales are places or sites where something happens, the way a spot is a location.

clue.text: Luxembourg's a capital

blocks.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
's can be short for has
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement that Luxembourg is a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks like is, naming Luxembourg the capital; read it as has instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Cheese melt, mean and hot, being cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cheese melt being cooked, mean-spirited in portion but served hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, much used for melting in fondue.
